Params: The airship touches down on the Balder's broad deck. Adelyde takes a thermal blanket from Aristo and, without a word, wraps it around you.
Before a word of thanks can leave your lips, Adelyde gently shakes her head.

Only now do you notice that the M.I.N.D. connection between you and Adelyde had seamlessly replaced Ananke's Link from the moment you returned to reality. Her thoughts flow steadily from the other end.
(I didn't expect you to be among the reinforcements sent to the Balder.)
(I didn't reach out ahead of time in case my signal was being tracked.)
(Kurono's people. When the submarine cables needed fixing, I hitched a ride on their ship to take care of some business. It's handled.)
Sorry to interrupt—yes, I can tell you two are having one of those silent exchanges that only a commandant and a Construct can have.
Can someone fill me in? Why did that armored lady go through all that trouble to snatch 【kuroname】, just to toss the commandant in the ocean?
Adelyde already scooped you up before we even sent the lifeboats.
(So my time spent in Ananke was only a moment on the outside.)
Rusalka... the armored lady you mentioned. Where is she now?
She dropped you and flew straight toward the Atlantic Eye. Did you scare her off?
Wait, that name... Rusalka... Rusalka Helio? Your teacher?
Didn't she go missing in the Atlantic Calamity and get declared dead?!
I'd like to know that myself.
There's been a lot of dead people coming back lately.
The pink-haired engineer lets out a sigh and scrubs his face with both hands as he often did when he was younger. Time really does favor some people.
The Balder has already broadcast an alert to every ship in the surrounding waters. They're told to keep their eyes open, hold position, and don't make any moves just yet.
Adelyde, deep in thought, furrows her brow and looks up to meet your gaze.
Think about what Rusalka said right before she dropped you.
Help us bring back the method to unravel the golden threads. Arius trusts you won't disappoint.

Since control of the submarine cables was reclaimed, global communications have been restored and all ships have reached the surrounding waters. Setting aside Rusalka's ambush, our operation has been proceeding smoothly.

If it's the better scenario, then Arius is genuinely wounded and out of commission, so we should press our advantage. But if it's the opposite... Is it possible our operation has been playing right into Arius' hands?
I don't like being led around by the nose like this.
But without Ananke's readings, going in blind would be too—
Gray Raven Commandant, transmission for you! The northern node forces have just linked up with the main fleet!
The comms lights up. Two faces appear on the other end with grave expressions, their eyes fixed on you.
Commandant, the operator said you were taken! What happened?
I knew it. My tracking device going haywire wasn't a malfunction.
(Great, they told them before I could even check in.)
There's no time for details right now. I need everyone to trust me.
Everyone, grab your detectors and set the parameters to these—
Aristo watches in disbelief as your fingers fly across the detector's interface. Data that only someone with Ananke's highest administrative access could know flows out without hesitation.
Ananke detection teams, run the tests now.
The readings match the radiation waves in the sea right now!
B-but calculating this would require an incredibly complex dynamic mathematical model...
Never mind how it happened! Are you seriously going to turn down solutions that fell out of the sky?!
Now that everything's in place, we have to get ahead of—
It's been years, and you've only grown more hard-working, Adelyde. Do you still want a compliment?
A voice clear as a whisper yet distant as a dream rises, and a chill colder than the frozen sea crawls up your spine. As one, everyone turns toward the Atlantic Eye.
The moment that voice rings out, Adelyde steps forward, putting herself between you and him.
Using her cannon as cover, she flings her terminal to Aristo, its screen showing two words only.
The curly-haired engineer bolts for the bridge the instant he makes out those two words. An equally brief message comes through the M.I.N.D. connection.
Before the great dam that looms like the skeleton of a leviathan, the Punishing Virus siphons into a dark crimson tornado, ascending and carrying its master to the sky in a baptism of blood.
The silver-white Ascendant claps three times ceremoniously, as if applauding the curtain fall on a well-staged play.
Why the hostility? I'm genuinely impressed by how quickly you resolved things this time.
It seems that with the right guidance, even kindling can burn bright.
Guidance? Since you crawled out of the grave you dug yourself, all you've done is cause trouble or play dead.
Death doesn't seem to have done anything for your parlance.
It at least taught me patience. Otherwise, you and your precious little commandant would be listening to me talk while drowning in the Red Tide right now.
Care to share why you're in such a good mood?
Even minds as dim as yours should have figured it out by now. This has always been about the "Understanding" Sefirah.
My truth. Born from my own hands, and shattered alongside me.
Half stolen away, hidden in the harbor's twilight rain; half buried deep, sealed within spacetime's threads of light.
(Can't he just speak plainly for once?)

Podesta's use of "Understanding" is as trivial as the difficulty to retrieve it, and the energy shortage is easily solved. The information flow through the submarine cables is enough to reawaken a dormant Sefirah.
The problem is the other half... Indeed, I cannot crack Dominik's Ananke.
He has plenty of experience getting in my way, and all the nerve of a repeat offender.
Fortunately, I know who can crack it.
You can feel his piercing gaze on you even across the distance.
A few decades ago, I watched two clockwork mice get wound up by Dominik with talk of morality and duty at the Atlantic Eye, then obediently scurry into Ananke to finish his last step for him.
If he could do it, why couldn't I? One orbital strike, and you all lined up to rush in and save the day, fishing the Sefirah out for me in the process.
Time is a scientist's greatest ally and greatest enemy. It bears witness to the outcome of every experiment... and in the end, it took my side.
The Red Tide directly beneath him suddenly comes to a boil.
Countless star-shaped drones tear through the crimson surface, trailing water as they rise into the air.
The Comet Patrol Array, which once guarded the Atlantic Eye till the end, now flickers with the red glow of the Punishing Virus between the seams of their armor.
Hundreds upon hundreds of calamity incarnates get into formation, their cannons charging and swiveling before locking onto every vessel converging on the Atlantic Eye.
By that logic, you shouldn't be using these infected Comet units to stop us at all. You should just let us through.
Two clockwork mice are enough. I have no use for a whole pack.
No one on this sea means anything to me, except for you and the Gray Raven Commandant.
And what you refuse to admit is that you mean just as little to the powers behind Babylonia and the TEC.

Human civilization has crumbled, and still they squabble over the scraps, purging anyone who gets in the way. Whoever ends up with the Atlantic Eye's legacy, it won't be any of you here who has a say in it.
The crew on deck are still preparing for battle with hurried steps, but the tension at the corners of their mouths suggests that Arius' poisonous words have seeped in.
—Why has Babylonia been at odds with the surface factions? Why does aid from the TEC never come easily?
—If those basking in the last light of the Golden Age had to pay a devastating price just to contain the disaster, what hope do those exhausted by the fight against the Punishing Virus have?
If you truly believe you've transcended humanity, what gives you the right to meddle with how humanity handles itself?
Arius lets out a wistful sigh.
Because the Atlantic Eye is my creation. From its conception to its demise, its fate belongs to me alone, and I will not have it desecrated.
And faster than those words is a laser beam streaking straight for Arius' neck from behind him.
The Ascendant barely dodges it. He turns, and every infected Comet unit turns with him, following his gaze.
Beneath a thousand blood-red stars, a single golden Comet rises slowly from beneath the dark ocean.
A Comet unit has been reset!
Blazing with a radiance never seen before, the drone unfurls its stellar rays and charges straight toward Arius—
The next instant, dozens of red beams pierce through it.
The eight-pointed star explodes into a burst of fire against the darkened sky in an instant. Yet, it captures the gaze of everyone across the entire fleet.
On the bridge of the Balder, Aristo anxiously draws a deep breath and opens the shipwide broadcast.
Attention, everyone. My name is Aristo. I'm an engineer assigned to the Balder.
That Comet unit just now was also called Aristo. Like me, it was the life's work of my mother, an Atlantic Eye engineer.
We engineers spend our days buried underwater without talking to anyone, and we love naming our work.
Every pipe, every steel beam in the Atlantic Eye... I wouldn't be surprised if each one has a name.
At that same moment, a progress bar pops up on every terminal aboard the Balder.
I doubt that Arius, the man who drafted the blueprints for the Atlantic Eye, knows how many coolant pipes are in a single Comet unit. But that's alright. I do.
I don't know the geometric tolerances of a hydro turbine guide bearing either, but that's alright. Someone does. The Atlantic Eye was built bit by bit that way.
Contributions come in different sizes. Assets have their owners. But does love have a hierarchy? Does pride have a pecking order?
Can Arius' love for the Atlantic Eye erase mine? Can his pride trample over mine?
A deep hum resonates through the hull. Adelyde clenches her fists, her head held high.
Aristo slams his fist on the edge of the control panel, and when he speaks again, every word lands like iron.
This is not for some grand cause or some great man. For my love and my pride—
I will not let my dreams become the devil's cradle.
Meanwhile\nEmergency War Council, Parliament Hall, Babylonia

A live feed projects into the center of the hall. The Balder's massive shield unfurls, cleaving through the Red Tide and sheltering the entire fleet behind as it charges toward the previously unreachable Atlantic Eye.
Within the dazzling blue-gold light, the unmistakable patterns of the <phonetic=M.I.N.D.>Phylotree</phonetic> emerge.
The hall erupts into heated discussion.
That shield alone could cover an entire conservation area...

Mass-producing Omega Devices has always been difficult, since there are never enough, and they're never ready in time. Now, even if we doubled the allocation for the Balder, we still wouldn't have pulled that off, right?
Could the Science Council have made a new technological breakthrough? There couldn't be a better moment for it!

A cold, clipped voice rises from Kurono's seat. The man with slicked-back, shoulder-length hair rests a clenched fist on the table, turning his gaze from the projection to the Science Council like a sweeping blade.

A critical strategic breakthrough achieved on the project that needed it most, unveiled at precisely the moment it was needed most, and yet somehow not a single person in this room had heard a word of it until now.

So which is it, Science Council? Have you been slacking through the development of the Omega File this whole time and just got lucky, or have you been sitting on this breakthrough for years and hiding it from this room?
He reaches out and points to the unmistakable markings on the shield.
We all have eyes. That is the pattern of the Phylotree, a program that the World Government and the Science Council buried together.
Despite its silent existence, unexplained concealment, and sudden reappearance, we still threw our full support behind the research and the scramble for Sefirah.
So tell me why is it that a technology that Babylonia doesn't have is now installed on a TEC vessel?

Without identifying himself, he speaks as "we," neatly sidestepping any challenge to his allegiances and steering the room's focus away from Kurono's grievances with the Science Council and onto an enemy from outside.
Who gets to know, and who doesn't? What gives them the right to have what we don't?
The Parliament goes still. Some wear frozen smiles on their faces as their eyes dart to the seats around them, while others furrow their brows over their terminals, their fingers typing fast.
At the center of every stare and whisper, Asimov does not so much as lift his head from his terminal. His eyes are fixed on the screen as he tracks the data streaming from the frontline.

Before everyone starts squabbling again over who gets a cut of technology none of you built, may I remind you: 90 percent of the forces aboard the Balder and the rest of that fleet are our own troops.
He raises a hand toward someone across the room with his palm up as a silent invitation.
As agreed, I handle the plan, and you handle everything else. Over to you, General Wells.
What does the General Staff have to do with any of this?
Were President Hassen and Commander Nikola informed of this?
The tactical resource negotiations with the TEC moved unusually fast once the General Staff got involved. Don't tell me—
Why don't we let the general explain it himself.
He cuts in to silence the room, his eyes narrowing slightly as his gaze drifts to his old colleague and new "partner," the same one he had just had a "productive working relationship" with.
(Could he have made a private deal with the TEC families on the side?)

(No way. Technology like this can rebuild a Clean Zone and reshape the balance of power. If he'd handed that over, the families wouldn't have held back the resources, and Kurono wouldn't have needed to intervene.)
(Wait... are they running a play against me together? But blowing everything up only hurts both sides, so what's the point?)
The figure in the ever-present military coat rises from his seat and walks into the holographic projection at the center of the hall. Everyone watches him, their expressions mixed.
Wells raises his head toward the President's seat at the central dais and meets Hassen's solemn gaze.
President Hassen, I hereby request ten minutes for a special address to the Parliament.
This is an emergency war council. Rules can wait.
Wells nods in acknowledgment, then turns toward the glowing shield in the projection.
Allow me to introduce the joint research initiative between the Science Council and the Watcher Society regarding the Omega File: Project Atlas.

This new Omega Shield, the "Atlas Shield", is not a breakthrough achieved by the Science Council alone, but rather the combination of the original Omega File with the Atlantic Eye's energy resonance technology.
To put it in terms everyone here cares about... this is the union of two classified technologies, each officially prohibited from being shared with the other.
Until today, only a handful of core developers on Babylonia and the TEC knew this existed.
The reason is simple: the moon rock strike alone proves that the poisonous snake has long been among us. What it's capable of is far worse than derailing a vital negotiation at the table.
The Chief of Staff, a man who usually keeps himself buried in battle plans and intelligence reports, lets his edge show for the first time, and his gaze sweeps across the shadows above.
That cold gleam appears briefly, but it is enough to silence the restless seats as he continues.
The discovery that these two technologies could be combined was, in fact, pure chance.
He raises a hand, gesturing toward the Balder in the projection, then to the Science Council.

Without ever accessing the Omega File, Watcher engineer Aristo discovered that whenever their energy resonance system was activated during the Balder modification project, the output of our Omega Weapons rose as well.
Meanwhile, our Chief Technician found within the files of the Phylotree of Ousia a series of research findings jointly authored by Dominik and Arius Erhorn.
The Atlantis Zero-point Reactor, the technology that ultimately gave birth to the Omega File, and the Atlantic Eye share a remarkably similar energy resonance design.
This leads to a frightening yet impossible to dismiss hypothesis: what if these two classified technologies were always meant to be two halves of the same whole?

Calamity and strife snapped the branch before the fruit ripened. The World Government and the TEC each gathered up the shattered pieces, both mistaking the broken halves for something that had never been whole.

We let division sever the bridge between science and progress, and we hid behind our walls and refused to speak with each other, as though that was simply the way of the world. But it was never meant to be.
A low murmur ripples through the seats. A councilman raises a hand.
A hypothesis is still just a hypothesis. Are you saying that alone was enough to convince the Chief of Staff to abuse his clearance and authorize this?
The state of this war speaks louder than any hypothesis.
How many times have we been held back by the limitations of our Omega Weapons? How many have we mourned because of those limitations?
I remember it all, because many of those impossible calls were mine to make. They were battle plans drafted by my own hand and resources allocated by my own order.
Every decision came after countless calculations. If there was any way to shave even a fraction of a percent off the Task Force's casualty rate, I would not let it slip by.
He opens his hand to reveal the red marks scored into his palm, and a small silver falcon insignia.
A Chief of Staff's duty is to remain rational, but as a soldier, protecting our people and reclaiming this earth is my calling. I refuse to accept it.
Are you implying that the rest of us have forgotten that calling?

Many of us here aren't without conviction, but we respect due process. Your words represent your views and nothing more. That doesn't make them right, nor does it mean we should support such a radical collaboration.
I understand. So, effective immediately, I will submit to any and all investigation.

The front lines can't afford to falter. My colleagues at the military command and the commandants fighting at the front have prepared thorough contingency plans. They are more than capable of completing the mission.
How are we supposed to trust the plans of someone like you?
He unpins the nameplate that marks him as Chief of Staff from his chest and walks to the center of the military's seats, setting it squarely on the table before Commander Nikola.
Nikola looks down at the nameplate and draws a slow, long breath.
But just as he opens his mouth, a voice rings out from beyond the doors, clear and bright as an open sky.
If his position can't be trusted, what about ours?
The heavy door to the Parliament Hall swings open. A woman in a silver-blue dress stands framed in the light, stepping inside with unhurried grace.
A member of Gray Raven, the first Construct to equip an Omega Core, and the first to bear the power of Sefirah... Even those who have never met her in person know her face and her story.
She stops on the far side of the projection, her gaze softening as it falls on the Balder. Then, she lifts her chin and looks out across the room.
To protect my Sefirah frame, I wasn't able to go to the front lines with my companions. Instead, I remained in Babylonia to assist in the development of Project Atlas.
The Task Forces on the front lines are not as in the dark about this debate as you might think.
They need to keep their focus, so they entrusted me to bring their voices from that battlefield to this one.
She takes out her terminal and projects a display in front of Balder's image.
It is a single phrase that has been signed by countless soldiers heading into battle, led by the signatures of 【kuroname】, the Gray Raven Commandant, and Adelyde, F.O.S. Instructor.
"I will always believe in the path that saves lives."
The man with graying hair looks up, fighting to hold back the warm tears threatening to spill from the corners of his eyes.
On the Eve of Adelyde's Departure for the Atlantic Eye
On the Eve of Adelyde's Departure for the Atlantic Eye, After the Second Atlantic Calamity
Her old F.O.S. Instructor finds her at Training Ground 004, a designation she has always had an inexplicable fondness for.
Wells sits on a crate, quietly waiting as she finishes her full drill simulation, stows her gun, and walks over to him.
At your pace, I'd end up in the Star of Life before the night's over.
He looks down at his hands. The gun calluses are gone, replaced by ones worn in from hours hunched over a desk. His fingers are still steady and strong, but his skin has grown rough and creased.
A tall silhouette blocks the light before him.
He looks up. Adelyde's face is almost unchanged from the day she first pushed open the door to his office. Time leaves no mark on her frame, only in her eyes.

She does not ask how the Chief of Staff with the weight of the world on his shoulders has found the time to show up at a training ground in the dead of night. She simply sits down on the crate beside him.
What does it feel like, sending your students to war and never seeing them come back?
An entire <phonetic=Silver Falcon>elite squad</phonetic> was decimated in such a simple mission, yet no one suspected any wrongdoing, not even me.
Was no one suspicious for real?
Is this belated justice even necessary...?
Feels like a piece of the best part of me died with them.
You're still not used to it after all these decades?
You've been an instructor for many years now. Have you gotten used to it?
The white-haired Construct goes quiet for a moment, then sighs.
The deal you made with Kurono was something we discussed together. I'll be using them to take care of a few things on my end, too, so don't trouble yourself over it.
As for the Atlantic Eye... you know how set I am on this. I have my reasons for going, and they aren't ones I can walk away from.
Though that's not the only reason I came to find you.
Tired as he is, the steel-blue eyes behind his lenses remain sharp and clear.
For this mission, you need to reach the Balder before the Atlas Shield activates.
Aristo will be there, but most of the crew aboard are Babylonia forces.

Once the Atlas Shield activates, I'll likely face a vote of no confidence within Babylonia. Even if I'm not stripped of operational command on the spot, my orders will carry a fraction of the weight they do now.
At a time like this, I need a commander on the frontline. Someone steadfast enough to rally people when it matters most.
You have one. 【kuroname】 is on that ship.
Project Atlas has only been disclosed to the core developers and the two of us liaisons.
...You can't be certain that the Gray Raven Commandant will still be willing to accept my appointment then.
Even without anyone asking, the commandant offers a hand when people need it most.
A faint smile crosses the Chief of Staff's perpetually taut face as he glances over at Adelyde.
That much faith in your own student?
Godspeed. May we win this fight.
Adelyde reaches out and shakes his hand firmly.
Wells stands up, stretching his stiff shoulders and neck. Nodding goodbye to Adelyde, he is nearly out the door when the red-clad Construct speaks up behind him.
You didn't send us to hell. Your Project Atlas gave everyone a chance to make it home.
Be proud of yourself, Wells. Wait for our return.
The notice of appointment for the new Atlantic Eye operation commander appears on every combatant's terminal, bearing the military's official seal.
In the distance, Arius pauses to study the patterns on the Atlas Shield for a moment.
It doesn't matter how, as long as you know the outcome.
See you at the Sefirah Engine.
With a dismissive wave, he steps into the Red Tide and sails toward the center of the dam, as if bored of the whole affair.
Against the wind sweeping across the sea, the Task Force Constructs stand at attention and salute you.
Commander Gray Raven, Lieutenant Colonel Adelyde, the aircraft to take you to the dam of the Atlantic Eye is ready!
